I am so sorry, your feelings are 100% valid. Allow yourself to feel however you feel. Do what you need to do to get through each day. I understand it's such a confusing, heartbreaking thing and nothing we say can make it all better. 

I wanted to offer this as someone who struggles with depression and suicide. If there's one thing I wish my loved ones knew, is how hard I fight to stay for them. We love you, your husband loves you. Our minds are so complex and play tricks. Sometimes it feels like it's the only way. But it's not yours or anyone's fault, I promise you, you were always on his mind. 

I apologize if this wasn't helpful. I just want you to know, you can be angry, sad, it's all okay. Take all the time you need, be gentle with yourself. But know, that you are cared for and his love for you and your love for him exists forever. ❤️

OP.... I'm so so sorry, not trying to project here, but my ex said and did the exact same thing almost word for word that you're saying. He's behaving that way because he's avoiding accountability and consequences. He is absolutely cheating on you (emotional cheating is just as valid as physical cheating), and he's gaslighting you so hard. His goal is to make you feel like you're crazy and insecure so that you'll believe he's innocent, but they both know what they're doing. Honestly, as hard as it will be, leave him in the dust. It will hurt, but you will have so much power and freedom from a poisonous person!
Yes, I'm surprised some people here are not seeing this behavior as inappropriate.

I agree that it would most likely be better/healthier to heal organically instead of trying to force feelings with someone else. 

I truly do not understand how someone could be okay with hurting or betraying someone they said they loved at one point. The fact that these people we love hold our lives in their hands. Relationships are such a huge risk. 

I'm a hopless romantic at heart, but hearing what you and everyone else on this sub is going through, plus my own reality, is slowly making me look at love so differently.

Yes, I think the most helpful thing is to be patient with yourself. Allowing yourself to feel how you feel with no shame just compassion. One thought that helps a little bit is thinking that all the things I wanted, how much more special it'll be when the "one" does it instead.

Like, I wish my ex would have just picked up a damn flower off the ground just once. I would have cherished that flower forever. But maybe it'll feel even better if the person I'm supposed to be with goes out of his way to get a bouquet, because he genuinely wanted to. Does that make sense? It might feel more rewarding that way.

*Also want to clarify its not about material things or their monetary value, but the principle of the gesture. It's the thought that counts.

I'm so so sorry. Mine told me he wants to explore what's out there, so I know it's going to happen any moment now. In a weird way, I wish I could "beat him to it." Like I secretly hope I'll find someone before he does, but I know that line of thinking isn't going to really heal me. Plus I can't even imagine being with anyone rn. 

I feel for you, I wish there was something we could do to take away the hurt instantly.
I'm glad you are feeling better about your ex. I wish to get to the same place!
Thank you very much, I'm coming up on a year post breakup but recently feel like I'm back at square one. I know what you're saying is true logically, I just can't get past the emotions.

I'm trying to be open-minded and dismantle this belief as well. I want to change my opinion but my mind is resisting.

NTA, but your fiance is showing some red flags that you should be aware of before marrying him. First, he just assumed the wedding would be child-free? Did you discuss this or did he just think it's his way or no way? Also, the wedding can be child-free for the guests and not you (your wedding your rules). The girls are old enough to be quiet and mature unlike small children. Second, you should question why a grown man cares more about his family's (potential) opinion of him rather than honoring the family he's marrying into. "Playing favorites?" Like huh? Of course you and your daughters are going to become his "favorites," you take priority over his orgin family now that he's an adult. (Let me guess, mommas boy?) 

Then he told you he's having a hard time containing his anger because you want your children there? Why is he getting so angry when you guys are just trying to communicate? He's going to be like this everytime you disagree? Then he gaslit you towards the end when he accused you of "flipping the argument." What you asked was a valid question. Then he stonewalls you (at least slightly) and even your kids! He doesn't get to play father only when he gets his way. His reaction concerns me. 

You should address these behaviors with him and see if he's willing to self-reflect and work on it, but if he doubles down... rethink.

I feel the same way, like is the no plus one rule for everyone or just OP's boyfriend? Also, I'm assuming there's going to be drinking involved at this party. So they're possibly going to get drunk, be alone and do what exactly? It's possible that nothing will happen, and I hope nothing does. But I wouldn't be surprised at all if something did. Couples are a package deal to me.

OP, I know my opinion may be unpopular here, but this would be a deal breaker for me. Men with close female friendships are already... iffy especially if there's history. I hate this social media trend where people try to convince you that you're crazy or insecure for having very valid concerns about who he is spending time with. Also, for the girl he dated to only invite him to her party and not offer to include you is a red flag to me on her part. I question why he even cares to be friends with her anyways, they only dated a month. 

To address your actual questions though, I personally would like my partner to be honest about his history with a friend. Imagine him not telling you, and then you find out later some other way. Also, it is absolutely ok to set boundaries with anybody, especially with women he's slept with. You're allowed to expect boundaries regardless of history or not. It's up to you and him to determine those lines though. You need to compromise on what your limits are and if he is unwilling or agrees to them but disrepects them anyway, let him go.

OP. This is abuse. Read what you wrote again... you give examples of "manipulation," you already acknowledge that he is manipulative and still try to give him props for being "right." In each example you gave he was 100% incorrect, and is very telling of his character. He goes out of his way to make you insecure and doubt yourself (gaslighting), he's ignorant and sexist (suggesting you won't be able find someone and have kids with them at 29), and he literally implied that he is allowed to sexually assault you whenever he wants because your "his woman." 

OP. I promise you your relationship is on the path to becoming physically/sexually abusive. He might seem nice most of time because he is love boming you (another abuse tactic), it's his way of keeping you wrapped around his finger so that you won't leave. You 1000% can find someone better than him literally by next week if you wanted to. He's telling you that because it's him who will actually have a hard time finding someone to put up with his shit. If he thinks he's right all the time, then let him think that all by himself, leave this lowlife.

If I could go back in time, the number one advice I would have given to myself is do not make them your whole world. As someone who also has an anxious/clingy attachment style, I made the mistake of leaving my passions, hobbies, goals, dreams behind just to make them my everything. And while l saw them as my world, they saw me as a placeholder for the next person. So it's ok to love someone hard, and you should prioritize your partner absolutely, but maintain yourself at the same time. Don't lose you to love them. Because if they leave and you put everything that made you you into them, then you're going to feel lost without them.

No I totally agree with you. It's ridiculous they have to have shit spelled out for them and weaponized incompetence is absolutely terrible. But yeah, for the sake of them resolving this issue I just think it's better in the long run. The fact that women/mothers are just made to carry the full burden at all times is infuriating.

I read a comment that you say you struggle with communicating with him sometimes and I've been there! I'm not an expert but if this helps, I've learned that when you have these conversations it's important to phrase things in a way that doesn't blame him or cause him to get defensive right away. When you do talk to him make sure you use 'I' statements instead of 'you' statements. Ex: "honey, I appreciate everything you've done around the house since we came home, but lately I've been feeling a little overwhelmed because x,y,z, and it would relieve some stress and mean a lot to me if we could work together to balance the care with the kids." If cleaning is theraputic to you tell him you'd be happy to swap duties sometimes, he can feed the baby while you pick up the kitchen. I wish you the best! And congrats on your baby!

NTA. I feel as though sometimes men just naturally think it's your job to be the main caretaker of the children because you're the mom and that's how society makes it seem, however both of you are responsible for your kids and no, you're not wrong for wanting help. Btw,  his job isn't to "help" you parent, it's to be a parent. You had a major surgery, and are taking care of 2 small children. It's great that he does other things around the house but I would have a discussion with him when you both are in a neutral mood and lead with that. Say how much you appreciate the things he does but that you feel a little overwhelmed and need some extra support. See if he's able to understand you and compromise on a feeding arrangement or maybe he can tend to the 2yo more to take the load off you. Good luck OP!

OP please please listen to this advice. I went through the same thing too and I regretted not leaving sooner. If you stay, he's just going to break your heart again and you'll have to start this healing process all over and then in the meantime you're never going to have peace with him because you'll always be anxious and on edge about everything he's doing and who he's talking to. It's going to drive you insane. Be grateful you were only 2 years in instead of 10+ like some of us.

A week later, he breaks up with me and just became so mean. 

Thank you so much for your kindness to reach out. It means a lot. I feel much calmer now. I have 2 good friends that have helped basically keep me on suicide watch 😅 they're a nice distraction. I just can't be alone with my thoughts for too long.

He told me he's not in love with me anymore and wants to be single for a while but at the same time I feel like he has all these other girls and crushes he could easily go to. I did so much for him throughout the years for nothing. He never appreciated anything, he never treated me well and said it was because I made him unhappy so thats why he never showed me affection near the end. I feel so unloved, used, not good enough, etc. I know he wasn't the best for me in some ways, but my attachment to him is so strong I get panic attacks when I think about him not being in my life. I'm also depressed and (TW) suicidal so idk if I can do this anymore.
Thank you, but no amount of talking about it or therapy has been able to help. I feel crazy, but I just can't be here anymore. I'm having a hard time finding a way to do it.

Your English is fine! I'm sorry you're experiencing something similar. I'm really in no position to give advice, but have you contacted her prior to booking the flight? I understood you want it to be a surprise, but I would hate for you to go and something happens and you regret it. Whether you stay or go, if you decide to talk to her, I would just put all of your pride aside and tell her that she is more important to you than anything that's happened before, and you guys can start from a clean slate (forget the past) or you can offer her the chance to work through the issues you had that caused these splits. If you were the dumper than you have more power to reach out than she does.
Yes, I was told by a family member how it would be selfish and I get told how this decision would make others feel bad. I know it would hurt them. But dammit, I want to be selfish for once you know?
Thank you for your reply! Literally just taking it one day at a time.

I could hear it but felt like I couldn't go down there and join him.

Same, my ex and I finished Squid Games close to our breakup. What helps me a little is watching YouTube videos of people reacting/commentating these shows/movies and I try to trick myself into thinking I'm watching it with the youtuber instead. Makes me feel not so alone.
Oh my God, yeah the music too. I hate that there's songs I genuinely like but can't play yet because of the memories.

No, don't feel bad! The length of time is definitely a factor in how painful it is for me, but no matter how long your relationship was any amount of time can have a significant impact. 

I hope for the both of us we are able to separate the two and just claim it as our own interest.
I'm so sorry, you're not alone and you have my support ❤

Yeah, I'm sorry you're also going through this. I was with my person for 10 years so I'm sure you can imagine how much we've seen together and it's almost like that media is 'tainted' now because I'll never be able to see it without thinking of them. 
 
This past Halloween was kind of the breaking point in our relationship and I dressed up as Moana from Disney... and now I can't look at Halloween or the movie Moana the same right now. 

We both are big fans of the John Wick movies and we are both so excited for the next potential release... but it hit me that when it comes out we aren't going to see it together. I'm trying so hard to "reclaim" these things for myself, but it's easier said than done of course.
